comparison: Both evaluate claims C38-C40 about EGFR specificity vs other RTKs. OpenEval finds the evidence SUPPORTED with appropriate controls. Peer review also finds this SUPPORTED, requesting only additional documentation of the genetic screen as a resource, not challenging the conclusions.

Both address C52 regarding negative results from EGF ligand over-expression. OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED as clearly documented negative results. Peer review marks UNCERTAIN, suggesting additional experiments (combining inhibitor knockdown with ligand over-expression) to test whether negative regulators override ligand effects.

Both evaluate C56, C75, C98 about EGFR activation causing transdifferentiation but not ectopic niche formation. OpenEval finds this SUPPORTED as important negative result. Peer review also finds SUPPORTED, with no challenges to this finding.

Both address ectopic niche formation claims C55, C74, C96. OpenEval finds evidence SUPPORTED with large sample sizes and statistical significance. Peer review marks UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 1 explicitly challenging the statistical conclusion, arguing the null hypothesis was not rejected and requesting more data or careful analysis.

Both evaluate Sprouty inhibition claims C44-C45, C49-C50. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with multiple lines of evidence. Peer review marks UNCERTAIN, requesting critical dpERK staining controls and compound knockdown experiments to determine if inhibitors act synergistically or through separate pathways.

Both address PTEN claims C46-C50. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED though notes direct biochemical evidence lacking. Peer review marks UNCERTAIN, questioning whether PTEN acts solely through EGFR inhibition and requesting dpERK controls and compound knockdown experiments.

Overlapping on C48 regarding PTEN mechanism. OpenEval finds the inference reasonable though indirect. Peer review challenges this interpretation, suggesting PTEN may indicate additional pathways participate, particularly without evidence that PTEN promotes EGFR degradation in the hub.

Both evaluate C51, C89 about Argos from cyst cells inhibiting EGFR. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED though notes the inference is indirect. Peer review marks UNCERTAIN, finding the model 'interesting' and 'supported from a genetics point of view' but noting the mechanism remains 'puzzling' and requesting localization studies.

Both address hub cell proliferation claims C33-C35, C37. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with converging evidence and appropriate controls. Peer review marks UNCERTAIN, questioning why EGFR activation produces lower mitotic percentages than downstream effectors, challenging whether EGFR is truly the 'master regulator.'

Both evaluate lineage tracing claims C33-C34, C43. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED by G-TRACE data. Peer review marks UNCERTAIN, noting a discrepancy where EGFR activation is less effective at driving mitosis but more effective at transdifferentiation in G-TRACE experiments.

Both address recovery after ablation claims C54, C73, C94-C95. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with gene dosage experiments and statistical significance. Peer review also finds SUPPORTED, with Reviewer 1 acknowledging the study is 'thoroughly and well documented' regarding EGFR's role in ablation-triggered transdifferentiation.

Both evaluate C53 about dpERK upregulation after CySC ablation. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with quantitative measurements and statistical significance. Peer review also finds SUPPORTED, with Reviewer 1 acknowledging the documentation of EGFR's role, though Reviewer 3 requests additional dpERK staining for inhibitor knockdowns.

Both address mechanistic model claims C63-C64, C67 about germ cells as EGF source. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED as reasonable and testable model though some elements inferential. Peer review marks UNCERTAIN, stating insufficient evidence to localize EGF source to germ cells and requesting compound ablation experiments.

Both address C41 about EGFR not required for hub cell maintenance. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with appropriate negative controls. Peer review also finds SUPPORTED with no challenges to this negative finding.
Both address C42 about Notch not involved. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with appropriate experimental design. Peer review also finds SUPPORTED with no challenges to this negative result.

Minimal overlap on C75. OpenEval evaluates C75, C76-C79 together as SUPPORTED inference about additional factors needed for ectopic niche formation. Peer review R8 addresses C75 in context of negative results from forced activation, finding this SUPPORTED.

Minimal overlap on C57. OpenEval finds summary claims C57-C60 SUPPORTED as appropriate conclusions from presented evidence. Peer review R1 questions the underlying data for C57 regarding EGFR as 'master regulator' given quantitative discrepancies.
Minimal overlap on C58. OpenEval finds summary claim C58 about inhibitors SUPPORTED. Peer review R2 questions the underlying inhibitor data, requesting additional controls and compound experiments.
Minimal overlap on C59. OpenEval finds summary claim C59 about ablation-triggered transdifferentiation SUPPORTED. Peer review R5 also supports the dpERK upregulation finding underlying this claim.
Minimal overlap on C60. OpenEval finds summary claim C60 about recovery SUPPORTED. Peer review R6 also supports the recovery data underlying this claim.
OpenEval evaluates background claims C1-C4, C10-C18 as SUPPORTED by appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background context claims.
OpenEval evaluates EGFR signaling background claims C25-C32, C82-C86 as SUPPORTED by appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.
OpenEval evaluates generalization claims C70-C72 about other systems as SUPPORTED with appropriate examples. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these comparative claims.
OpenEval evaluates prior research background claims C19-C24 as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background claims.
OpenEval evaluates C61 as UNCERTAIN, noting it is explicitly speculative and untested. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this speculative claim.
